findings.reason: a node implementing the key exactly as written either fails its own changed-file gate or ships a cache that serves stale resource metadata after an edit, so the key (or the done-when) must be restated to include per-file signatures.
findings.text: s8's deliverable keys the reused resource scan on "the tree signature the metadata index already uses for its walk-skip (§3)", but that signature is the directory entry-set identity: `_dir_identity` (reckon/metadata_index.py:563) explicitly returns "the stat identity a directory's entry set changes with … mtime and ctime move when an entry is added to or removed", and `_reuse_covered` (metadata_index.py:215) reuses only when every recorded directory is unchanged. Editing a plan file's bytes leaves its directory's mtime/ctime/inode/size unchanged, so a key drawn from the walk-skip cannot see a content edit, yet s8's deliverable says "a changed file invalidates it" and its done-when requires "a changed file makes the next read scan again". The index detects content change only by a separate per-file rehash (`index_rows(revalidate=True)` rehashes every covered file after the walk-skip) — a step s8's stated key omits — so a scan cached under the walk-skip signature would return a stale `content_digest`/resource set after an edit.

findings.reason: §7's landing was closed without resolving f-araiid-005 or writing its successor, so a `/reckon-build` driven off the followup list would dispatch completed work and never reach §8/§9.
findings.text: the only open followup `f-araiid-005` (data-status="open", data-recommends-skill="/reckon-build a-read-answers-inside-its-deadline §7") dispatches §7, which the plan now records as `data-status="done"` (c-close-s7, 2026-10-13), while the two remaining implementable sections §8 (`data-status="implementable"`) and §9 (`data-status="implementable"`) are named by no followup.
